name: Carrion Defense Works Harvester CDW-12 'Thresher'
description:
A man-portable flechette support weapon that fires dense clouds of 2mm steel flechettes at a cyclic rate sufficient to saturate a 10-meter wide corridor with lethal projectiles. The Harvester uses a multi-stage electromagnetic accelerator fed from a backpack-mounted flechette hopper containing 8,000 rounds.

Carrion Defense Works designed the Thresher for corridor clearing operations — the close-quarters nightmare scenarios inside GLMZ's dense urban superstructures where conventional support weapons are too slow to track fast-moving threats in tight spaces. The CDW-12's flechette cloud does not require precision aiming; the operator simply points the weapon in the direction of the threat and lets the statistical spread ensure hits.

The Thresher's lethality comes from volume rather than individual round energy. A single flechette might not penetrate heavy armor, but a cloud of 200 flechettes fired in a half-second burst will find every gap, seam, and joint in any protective system. Medical teams recovering bodies from Thresher engagements describe the results as 'difficult to identify.'
legality: Military restricted — antipersonnel area weapons authorization
specifications:
caliber: 2mm steel flechette
effective_range: 10-100 meters
rate_of_fire: 4,000 flechettes per minute
capacity: 8,000-round backpack hopper
weight: 6.8 kg weapon, 12 kg loaded hopper
power_source: Backpack capacitor, 2,000 flechettes per charge cycle
tactical_use: The Thresher is deployed in close-quarters environments where precision is less important than total coverage. Corridor clearing, room breaching, and tunnel operations are its primary applications. The weapon's flechette spread pattern can be adjusted from a tight 5-degree cone to a wide 30-degree fan depending on the engagement environment. Operators describe using the CDW-12 as 'painting' a space with steel — every surface within the engagement zone receives multiple impacts.
cultural_context: Carrion Defense Works has earned a reputation for weapons that prioritize lethality over precision, and the Harvester is their most extreme expression of this philosophy. Humanitarian organizations have repeatedly called for a ban on flechette cloud weapons, citing the indiscriminate nature of area-saturation fire. Carrion's legal defense argues that the weapon reduces collateral damage by confining lethality to a defined engagement zone — a claim that requires a very specific definition of 'collateral.'
story_hooks: A Thresher was used in a residential corridor dispute, saturating a section of Tier 2 housing with flechettes. Fourteen people died, including six who were in adjacent rooms when the flechettes penetrated thin interior walls. The operator claims they were told the area was evacuated.

Carrion is developing a flechette variant that carries a micro-payload of incapacitating agent on each dart — turning the Thresher from a lethal weapon into a theoretically non-lethal area denial tool. Field tests suggest the dosage calculation needs work.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist handheld projector resembling a cross between a construction tool and a military support cannon. Compact rectangular body with aggressive angular lines, tapering forward into a flared muzzle housing. Mounted atop a robust harness frame that connects to an external backpack module. Overall impression is industrial efficiency — form follows lethal function.
physical_description.dimensions: Weapon body: 62cm length × 14cm width × 18cm height. Barrel projection: 28cm. Muzzle aperture: 8cm diameter. Backpack hopper: 35cm × 25cm × 20cm
physical_description.weight_description: The handheld unit feels deceptively light (6.8kg) due to efficient polymer construction, but the fully-loaded backpack harness (12kg additional) creates substantial shoulder and back burden. Weight distributes through wide shoulder straps and hip brace.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame with integrated steel reinforcement ribs. Electromagnetic accelerator housing: hardened steel. Hopper: layered carbon-composite with internal steel baffles for flechette regulation.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal grey with brushed steel accents around the muzzle and capacitor coupling points. High-wear areas show bare composite where paint has been stripped by repeated use. Faint scorch marks around discharge aperture.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: industrial grey-black composite. Accents: brushed steel, copper-colored capacitor terminals. Warning striping: safety yellow-orange around power coupling and hopper feed mechanism.
physical_description.grip_texture: Wrapped in textured non-slip polymeric tape, worn smooth by gloved hands. Sharp angular edges along trigger guard and selector switches provide tactile feedback for fingering controls even in combat pressure suits.
distinctive_features: Flared bell-shaped muzzle housing with visible electromagnetic coil rings
Three-axis spread-pattern adjustment dial mounted on left side
Integral cooling vents in rows along barrel housing
Bright amber LED charge indicator (pulses during cycling)
Cable connector assembly linking weapon to backpack: heavy industrial-grade coupling
Pressure-relief valve venting on rear of hopper with safety interlock
Tactical rail system along top for auxiliary optics (most operators omit — flechette spread eliminates precision aiming)
Impact scars and micro-fractures in composite from spent flechette ricochet
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CARRION DEFENSE WORKS logo stamped in raised relief on left side of weapon body (3cm). Serial number etched into steel charging plate. Manufacturing date code (2221) visible on hopper assembly. Multilingual warning labels in English and Mandarin on backpack frame.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-deployed units show heavy wear: composite dulled by handling, muzzle housing scorched, minor dents from transport impacts. Hopper mounting brackets show corrosion from indoor urban humidity. Most units display amateur maintenance marks and improvised grip tape repairs. Battle-scarred specimens show impact cratering from stray fire or ricochet.
